task.description: HARD GATE. Independently validate REQ-027's test design (commits 07ff7fe, 569f2e4) against WF-02 Step 3b's checklist (a)-(e) and REQ-027's five acceptance criteria. Read the spec and test sources directly -- never TEST-DESIGNER's result.summary as a substitute. The central question is not whether a test exists per criterion but whether it would actually FAIL if the criterion were violated: hunt vacuous passes. One normalization subtlety is flagged in the dispatch prompt and must not be misread as a weakened check.
acceptance_criteria: every one of REQ-027's 5 acceptance criteria has at least one runnable test that demonstrably fails when the criterion is violated, verified by mutation where practical
no @tag :skip without a passing counterpart, and no TODO left in the spec
fixtures use per-test unique data; no cross-test pollution; tests are self-sufficient and order-independent
no hardcoded secrets or connection strings; no wall-clock or unseeded-randomness dependence
the async: true / async: false split is sound given ISS-0011's documented flake mode
every tenant schema a test creates is dropped, including on the failure path

result.summary:
PASS. All five of REQ-027's acceptance criteria (grepped verbatim from docs/requirements.yaml:1188-1192, not taken from TEST-DESIGNER's summary) have at least one runnable test that demonstrably FAILS when the criterion is violated. Verified by TEN mutations against a real Postgres partition (MIX_TEST_PARTITION=2 -> letflow_test2), each reverted with `git diff` confirmed empty afterwards. Baseline before mutating: `MIX_TEST_PARTITION=2 mix test test/letflow/definitions/schemas_test.exs test/letflow/definitions/migrations_test.exs` -> `Result: 36 passed` (migrations_test 14, schemas_test 22).

=== PER-CRITERION MAPPING AND MUTATION EVIDENCE ===

AC1 -- "priv/repo/migrations gains process_definitions and instance_definition_snapshots migrations, both schema-per-tenant via REQ-022's :prefix mechanism, applying cleanly".
Covering tests: migrations_test.exs:285 (replay applies both, both land in tenant schema), :309 (both registered in tenant_scoped_migrations/0), :326 (column set == __schema__(:fields)); schemas_test.exs:395 (no compile-time @schema_prefix); plus event_store/migrations_test.exs:493 (the §4 guard test, which iterates tenant_scoped_migrations/0 -- now nine entries including REQ-027's two).
MUT-2b: deleted the CreateInstanceDefinitionSnapshots tuple from lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning.ex's manifest. 6 failures, `Result: 30/36 passed`, including verbatim:
  "4) test ... tenant_scoped_migrations/0 registers both REQ-027 definition migrations
      test/letflow/definitions/migrations_test.exs:309
      Letflow.Repo.Migrations.CreateInstanceDefinitionSnapshots is not registered in tenant_scoped_migrations/0 -- it would never reach any tenant schema"
and migrations_test.exs:285 / :326 / :547 / :572 / :618 all failed alongside.
MUT-2a (the actual :prefix-mechanism gate): changed `if prefix() do` to `if true do` in 20260816193001_create_process_definitions.exs. `Result: 12/13 passed`, verbatim:
  "1) test §4 guard pattern -- every registered tenant-scoped migration is a real no-op without a prefix ...
      test/letflow/event_store/migrations_test.exs:493
      a registered tenant-scoped migration created something in public when run with no :prefix -- §4's guard pattern is missing or broken in one of: [... Letflow.Repo.Migrations.CreateProcessDefinitions, Letflow.Repo.Migrations.CreateInstanceDefinitionSnapshots]"
That run also emitted `DROP TABLE IF EXISTS "public"."process_definitions" CASCADE` from that test's on_exit -- i.e. Step 2d carry-forward (c)'s @later_tenant_scoped_tables addition was exercised for real and did its job. This is the only mutation in this session that could have stranded a stray public table, and it did not.
See issue TDV-027-01 below for a MINOR, non-blocking finding about one belt-and-braces assertion inside migrations_test.exs:285.

AC2 -- "process_definitions has a unique index on (name, version) and a partial unique index on name WHERE status = 'active'".
Covering tests: migrations_test.exs:348 (uq_definition_version total UNIQUE over exactly (name, version), no WHERE), :370 (duplicate rejected as {:error, changeset}), :405 (uq_active_definition PARTIAL unique over (name), predicate derived from Ecto.Enum), :437 (behavioural PD-03); schemas_test.exs:223 (both constraints declared by index name).
MUT-4 (the flagship -- enum/predicate case drift): `where: "status = 'active'"` -> `where: "status = 'ACTIVE'"`. Exactly the two intended tests failed, verbatim:
  "2) test ... uq_active_definition is a PARTIAL unique index over (name) whose predicate matches the literal Ecto.Enum actually dumps for :active
      test/letflow/definitions/migrations_test.exs:405
      uq_active_definition's predicate is ((status)::text = 'ACTIVE'::text), but Ecto.Enum dumps :active as \"active\" -- the index would match ZERO rows and PD-03 would be silently unenforced"
  "1) test ... a second definition activated under a name that already has an active definition is rejected by uq_active_definition (PD-03)
      test/letflow/definitions/migrations_test.exs:437
      ** (MatchError) no match of right hand side value:
          {:ok, %Postgrex.Result{command: :update, ..., num_rows: 1, ...}}
      code: assert {:error, %Postgrex.Error{postgres: postgres}} = activate(schema_name, second.id)"
The second activation SILENTLY SUCCEEDED (num_rows: 1) under the drifted predicate -- exactly the zero-row-matching-index failure mode carry-forward (a.2) exists to gate, caught behaviourally as well as structurally.
MUT-3: added `where: "status = 'draft'"` to uq_definition_version -> "1) ... uq_definition_version is a total UNIQUE index over exactly (name, version) / migrations_test.exs:348 / code: assert index_predicate(definition) == nil". The "no WHERE clause" half has teeth.

AC3 -- "process_definitions has a nullable stage column and a partial index on stage WHERE stage IS NOT NULL".
Covering tests: migrations_test.exs:486 (nullable + omitted stage lands as SQL NULL), :509 (idx_def_stage non-unique PARTIAL on (stage)); schemas_test.exs:343 (castable, optional, length-only, no enum).
MUT-5a: `add :stage, :string` -> `add :stage, :string, null: false, default: ""` ->
  "3) ... stage is a nullable column and an omitted stage lands as SQL NULL ... / migrations_test.exs:486 / process_definitions.stage is NOT NULL -- PD-07 requires it nullable so existing rows need no back-fill"
MUT-5b: removed `where: "stage IS NOT NULL"` from idx_def_stage ->
  "4) ... idx_def_stage is a non-unique PARTIAL index over (stage) predicated on stage IS NOT NULL / migrations_test.exs:509 / idx_def_stage has no WHERE clause -- it indexes NULL entries too ...: CREATE INDEX idx_def_stage ON tenant_460cf...process_definitions USING btree (stage)"

AC4 -- "instance_definition_snapshots.definition_id references process_definitions.id with no ON DELETE CASCADE, and the moduledoc states this is deliberate per PD-08".
Covering tests: migrations_test.exs:547 (pg_constraint.confdeltype), :572 (behavioural delete rejection + snapshot survives with its graph), :618 (dangling FK as {:error, changeset}); schemas_test.exs:144 (moduledoc), :166 (FK constraint name), :188 (write-once API), :203 (no belongs_to).
MUT-6: `on_delete: :nothing` -> `on_delete: :delete_all`. Both halves fired, verbatim:
  "2) ... the snapshot FK's referential action in the live catalog is NO ACTION ('a'), not CASCADE ('c') / migrations_test.exs:547 / the snapshot FK's ON DELETE action is \"c\", expected \"a\" (NO ACTION) per PD-08"
  "1) ... deleting a definition that has a snapshot row is rejected, and the snapshot survives with its captured graph (PD-08) / migrations_test.exs:572 / Expected exception Ecto.ConstraintError but nothing was raised"
MUT-9 (moduledoc half of AC4): "This is deliberate, per PD-08" -> "This is intentional, per PD-08" ->
  "1) ... InstanceDefinitionSnapshot's moduledoc states the missing ON DELETE CASCADE is deliberate per PD-08 / schemas_test.exs:144 / Assertion with =~ failed"
RE-DERIVED CLAIM (confirmed): pg_constraint.confdeltype IS the only place the action is observable. `on_delete: :nothing` is the %Reference{} struct default and falls through the Postgres adapter's catch-all `reference_on_delete(_), do: []`, so the emitted DDL carries no ON DELETE clause at all and pg_get_constraintdef renders nothing to assert on. Reading confdeltype::text and asserting "a" with a companion `refute == "c"` is correct and is the only non-vacuous formulation available.

AC5 -- "both Ecto.Schema modules' @moduledoc cite R-Co src/design/definition.md (PD-01/PD-07/PD-08 sections) as the ported source".
Covering tests: schemas_test.exs:98, :116.
MUT-7 (first attempt, RECORDED AS A NEGATIVE RESULT): changing one "and the PD-07 section" phrase in ProcessDefinition's moduledoc did NOT fail the test, because PD-07 is cited several times in that moduledoc and the assertion is a substring match. That is correct behaviour for a criterion phrased as "cite ... the PD-07 section", not a weakness -- but it is why a single-occurrence mutation is not a valid probe here.
MUT-7b (decisive): `sed 's/PD-07/PD-7/g'` across lib/letflow/definitions/process_definition.ex ->
  "1) test acceptance criterion 5 -- ported-source citations both definition schema modules' moduledocs cite R-Co's src/design/definition.md and its PD-01, PD-07 and PD-08 sections
      test/letflow/definitions/schemas_test.exs:98
      Letflow.Definitions.ProcessDefinition's moduledoc does not cite the PD-07 section"
The assertions read the compiled Docs chunk via Code.fetch_docs/1 and pattern-match the {:docs_v1, ..., %{"en" => moduledoc}, ...} shape, so a deleted (:none) or hidden (:hidden) moduledoc raises rather than passing vacuously -- verified by reading normalized_moduledoc/1 at schemas_test.exs:53-58.

=== THE NORMALIZATION SUBTLETY: ASSESSED ON THE MERITS, JUDGED A STRENGTHENING ===
Confirmed empirically: Postgres renders the predicate as ((status)::text = 'active'::text), never as the criterion's literal `status = 'active'` (seen in MUT-4's own failure message and in MUT-5b's CREATE INDEX dump). A verbatim assertion of the criterion's wording would therefore fail against a fully correct schema -- it would be a broken test, not a strong one. TEST-DESIGNER's response (derive the expected literal from Ecto.Enum.mappings(ProcessDefinition, :status)[:active] and assert `predicate =~ "'#{active_literal}'"`, with separate assertions that the predicate exists at all and that it names `status`) is STRONGER than a hard-coded 'active', and I concur with ORCH's read. Two independent reasons, both verified rather than argued: (1) it cannot go stale -- a future change to the enum's dumped case fails the test instead of silently invalidating it, which a hard-coded literal would not; (2) MUT-4 proves it is bidirectionally sensitive -- I mutated only the MIGRATION side and the test failed with a message naming both sides. The decomposition into three assertions (predicate non-nil / names status / carries the derived literal) means a failure is diagnosable rather than a bare regex miss. This is NOT a weakened check and I did not score it as one.

=== ASYNC SPLIT: SOUND ===
ISS-0011's root cause (re-read from docs/issues/ISS-0011.yaml including all three UPDATE blocks) is an `async: true` module calling a GLOBAL `:telemetry.attach` for [:letflow, :repo, :query] and then `refute_received` -- so a concurrently running async test's own Repo query lands in its window. The precondition is (async: true) AND (global telemetry handler) AND (other async tests issuing Repo queries).
schemas_test.exs (async: true) is verified structurally clean: `grep -n "telemetry\|Repo\|DataCase"` returns exactly three hits, ALL of them prose inside comments/moduledoc (lines 12, 14, 205). It attaches no handler, checks out no connection, uses ExUnit.Case rather than Letflow.DataCase, and issues zero Repo calls -- so it can neither repeat the mistake nor supply the foreign query events the flake trips on. Its 22 tests run in 0.2s.
migrations_test.exs is async: false for the whole module, which is what makes its Sandbox.mode(:auto) switch safe (ExUnit drains all async modules before any sync module and runs sync modules one at a time). The :auto switch would be actively unsafe under async: true, so the split is not stylistic -- it is required. This mirrors the established pattern in event_store/migrations_test.exs, tenant_provisioning_test.exs and registry_test.exs.
Caveat noted, not new and not blocking: the module sets Sandbox.mode(:auto) in setup and never restores it. That is the pre-existing project-wide pattern (event_store/migrations_test.exs:205,456; tenant_provisioning_test.exs:345,396; registry_test.exs:155), and DataCase's own setup re-establishes {:shared, self()} for every subsequent non-async test, so it self-heals. REQ-027 neither introduces nor worsens it.

=== CLEANUP: VERIFIED, INCLUDING THE FAILURE PATH ===
on_exit registration order confirmed by reading migrations_test.exs:262-274: provision_tenant_schema/1 is asserted first, THEN on_exit(drop_schema! + delete Registration + delete Tenant) is registered, THEN replay_migrations/2 is asserted. So the cleanup is armed before the only step that can realistically raise.
MUT-10 proved this empirically rather than by reading: I injected `raise "MUTATION-FORCED REPLAY FAILURE"` into the body of 20260816193002 so replay_migrations/2 raises inside setup. Every test in the describe block failed with `message: "MUTATION-FORCED REPLAY FAILURE"` AND every one of them still emitted its `DROP SCHEMA IF EXISTS "tenant_..." CASCADE`. The failure path is genuinely covered.
Post-run database audit against letflow_test2 (confirmed via SELECT current_database() -> "letflow_test2"; letflow_test and letflow_dev were never touched), taken AFTER all ten mutation runs and two full-suite runs:
  tenant_% schemas: []   stray public.process_definitions / public.instance_definition_snapshots: []   tenant_schemas rows: 0   tenants rows: 0
  public contains only: approvals, groups, schema_migrations, tenant_role, tenant_schemas, tenants, transition_events, users (the legitimate non-tenant-scoped set).

=== STEP 3b CHECKLIST (a)-(e) ===
(a) Runnable test per criterion, no @tag :skip without a passing counterpart -- PASS. All five criteria mutation-verified above. `grep -niE "@tag :skip|TODO|FIXME|:pending"` across both test files and the spec: no hits.
(b) No "TODO: implement test" in the spec -- PASS. Same grep; the only hit in test/specs/REQ-027.md is line 339's own claim "No @tag :skip, no TODO", which is itself true.
(c) Per-test unique fixtures, no cross-test pollution -- PASS. Each DB test gets its own Tenant (slug "req027-#{System.unique_integer([:positive, :monotonic])}"), its own physical Postgres schema and its own Registration row, all minted in a per-test setup; definition names use the same VM counter. schemas_test uses Ecto.UUID.generate/0 + unique_integer with no shared mutable state. Corroborated empirically: zero orphan schemas and zero leftover tenant/registration rows after ten mutation runs including several with 4-6 failing tests.
(d) Self-sufficient / order-independent -- PASS. No test reads state another test wrote; every fixture is created in setup. Corroborated across runs at differing seeds (observed seed 773488 among others) and by MUT-2b/MUT-10 where partial failure of the block left the surviving tests' outcomes unchanged.
(e) No hardcoded secrets or connection strings -- PASS. `grep -niE "password|postgres://|ecto://|localhost|5432|5462|secret|api[_-]?key"` across both test files: no hits in code (one prose hit at test/specs/REQ-027.md:337 asserting their absence). Both files reach Postgres only via Letflow.Repo, configured from config/test.exs.
PLUS: no wall-clock dependence -- `grep -niE "utc_now|:rand\.|Enum.random|System.system_time|:os.timestamp"` returns only a comment at migrations_test.exs:58 explaining their absence; timestamps are the fixed literal ~N[2026-01-02 03:04:05.000000]. No unseeded randomness -- uniqueness is System.unique_integer([:positive, :monotonic]) (a VM counter) and Ecto.UUID.generate/0.

=== event_store/migrations_test.exs: CLEANUP-LIST-ONLY CHANGE CONFIRMED ===
`git show 07ff7fe -- test/letflow/event_store/migrations_test.exs` is +25/-5 across exactly two hunks: (1) a new @later_tenant_scoped_tables module attribute listing the two REQ-027 table names, plus its explanatory comment; (2) inside the §4 guard test's on_exit, `for table <- Map.keys(@event_store_tables)` becomes `cleanable = Map.keys(@event_store_tables) ++ @later_tenant_scoped_tables; for table <- cleanable`, with the adjacent comment reworded. NO assertion in that file was added, removed, weakened or otherwise changed -- the guard test's `assert public_tables() == tables_before` at :514 is byte-identical, and it already covered REQ-027 because it iterates tenant_scoped_migrations/0. MUT-2a exercised both the assertion (it failed and named CreateProcessDefinitions) and the new cleanup entry (it dropped the stray public.process_definitions), so the change is proven necessary and proven harmless.

=== OTHER RE-DERIVED CLAIMS ===
AC2 behavioural fixture (asked to be re-derived): VERIFIED that the partial index really is the discriminator. migrations_test.exs:445-446 inserts two rows with the SAME name and DIFFERENT versions ("1.0.0", "2.0.0"), so uq_definition_version cannot be what rejects; both are asserted status == :draft at :452-453, and their coexistence is only possible under a PARTIAL index -- a total unique index on (name) would have made the second Repo.insert! raise before the test ever reached its activation step. The stored value is then read straight out of the column with no Ecto load in between (:458-464) and only afterwards is the first row activated. The final rejection is pinned to postgres.code == :unique_violation AND postgres.constraint == "uq_active_definition", so a rejection by any other constraint would not satisfy it. The test proves what it claims.
graph-default guard (asked to be re-derived): VERIFIED the `refute is_nil(column_default)` guard genuinely blocks a vacuous pass. MUT-8 changed `add :graph, :map, null: false, default: %{"nodes" => [], "edges" => []}` to a bare `add :graph, :map` and the guard fired first, verbatim:
  "2) ... the DB column default for graph and the schema module's struct default are the same value / migrations_test.exs:645 / process_definitions.graph has no DB default at all -- the migration's default: %{\"nodes\" => [], \"edges\" => []} is missing / code: refute is_nil(column_default)"
The surrounding design is sound: the row is created by a raw INSERT that omits `graph` (so the DATABASE default fills it), read back through the schema module, compared against %ProcessDefinition{}.graph, and then separately pinned to the literal %{"nodes" => [], "edges" => []} so both sides agreeing on a WRONG value still fails.

=== SUITE STATE ===
Full suite on the restored tree: `MIX_TEST_PARTITION=2 mix test` -> `Result: 307 passed (4 properties, 303 tests)`, Finished in 33.7s. Exactly the stated baseline. No ISS-0011 occurrence in this run; no other failure at any point in this session that was not one I deliberately injected.

=== TREE STATE ===
Every mutation was reverted with `git checkout --` and the tree re-verified: `git diff --stat` is EMPTY and `git status --short` shows only `?? handoffs/WF02-REQ027-20260816/step-03b-test-design-validator.json` (this file). No test code, application code, migration or design artefact was modified by this gate. Branch feature/WF02-REQ027-20260816 throughout; never switched, never touched main, never ran docker compose up, never touched the sibling worktree, letflow_test, letflow_dev or ai-dala-infra.

VERDICT: PASS. No check in (a)-(e) failed, and all five acceptance criteria are gated by tests proven to fail on violation. One MINOR, non-blocking observation and one MINOR spec-accuracy note are recorded in result.issues -- neither is a check failure and neither is grounds for rework.

issues.title: migrations_test.exs:300's `refute table_exists_in_schema?("public", table)` cannot fire under the replay_migrations/2 path; its comment and the spec overstate what it proves
issues.detail:
test/letflow/definitions/migrations_test.exs:300-301 refutes that either REQ-027 table exists in `public`, commented "This half is what proves :prefix is doing the work"; test/specs/REQ-027.md:111-113 repeats the claim. Under replay_migrations/2 that assertion is structurally guaranteed and cannot fail. Ecto.Migration.__prefix__/1 (deps/ecto_sql/lib/ecto/migration.ex:1757-1771) injects the migrator's prefix into any table/index struct whose own :prefix is nil, and RAISES ("the :prefix option `...` does not match the migrator prefix `...`") when an explicit prefix disagrees -- so with a migrator prefix set, this DDL can only land in the tenant schema. Confirmed by mutation MUT-1: replacing every `prefix: prefix()` with `prefix: nil` in BOTH REQ-027 migrations left all 14 tests green (`Result: 14 passed`).

Why this is MINOR and not a gate failure: AC1 is not dependent on that assertion. Its positive half (`assert table_exists_in_schema?(schema_name, table)`) does fire -- MUT-2b failed it with "instance_definition_snapshots is missing from tenant schema tenant_...". And the genuine :prefix-mechanism gate for AC1 is the `if prefix() do` guard, which IS exercised, by test/letflow/event_store/migrations_test.exs:493's §4 guard test that iterates tenant_scoped_migrations/0 (now nine entries) -- MUT-2a made that test fail and it named CreateProcessDefinitions in its candidate list. So AC1 has two independent, mutation-proven failing paths.

Suggested (non-blocking, for a future run -- NOT rework of this step): soften the two comments to say the refute is defence-in-depth against a hard-coded wrong prefix, and point at event_store/migrations_test.exs:493 as the assertion that actually proves the guard. No test code change is needed.

issues.title: test/specs/REQ-027.md enumerates 20 AC-mapped cases but the two files ship 36 test functions
issues.detail: migrations_test.exs contains 14 tests and schemas_test.exs 22, totalling 36 (matching the commit message's "+36 new tests" and the 271 -> 307 suite delta). The spec's numbered list covers 20 of them -- the AC-mapped ones -- while the remainder (schemas_test.exs's "changeset validations (pure, no I/O)" describe block, the primary-key/source/association assertions, and migrations_test.exs's status-default test) are real, passing, non-skipped coverage that the spec does not enumerate. Extra coverage beyond the spec is not a gap and no acceptance criterion is left unmapped, so this is a documentation-completeness note only. Suggested for a future run: add a one-line "supporting coverage not enumerated above" note to the spec's Coverage check section.
